explain: Devlinks is a browser-local editor with no settings; hosted accounts and public profile pages switch on only where all five AUTH_* settings exist (today only as Preview values scoped to the feat/breakthrough-accounts branch, which `check` ignores, so it reports them missing until they move to the unscoped Preview), and installs need a read-only GitHub Packages token.

env.why: This deployment's exact https origin. The issuer only returns sign-ins to the callback registered for it; with any AUTH_* value missing, accounts stay off and the editor is browser-local.
env.agentFix: Set to the Preview deployment's stable https origin, the one registered as the client's callback on accounts-preview.royeradames.com.

env.why: Signs this app's own session cookies (32 or more characters). Changing it signs everyone out of Devlinks.
env.agentFix: Generate 32 random bytes in memory and add with vercel env add --sensitive, never printed (as royer-auth connect-app.mjs does).

env.why: The central Breakthrough sign-in issuer. The app checks it is exactly <origin>/api/auth.
Identifies Devlinks to the issuer. Without it, accounts stay off.
env.agentFix: Register the app with royer-auth connect-app.mjs (operator automation token on the Mac), which writes the client ID to Vercel.

env.why: Proves to the issuer that the token request comes from Devlinks. Without it, sign-in fails at the callback.
env.agentFix: connect-app.mjs mints it at registration and writes it as Sensitive without printing; rotate by re-registering.

env.readBy: .npmrc reads ${NPM_TOKEN} when npm installs @royeradames/auth from GitHub Packages.
env.why: Installs the private @royeradames/auth package from GitHub Packages through the committed .npmrc. Without it, npm ci and every Vercel build fail.
env.whyHuman: GitHub Packages needs a classic personal access token minted inside Royer's GitHub account; agents can't create tokens for him.

steps: Open the link signed in as royeradames. It preselects read:packages only, because installs need nothing more.
Set an expiry (90 days) so a leaked token stops working on its own, then Generate token.
In your own Terminal, run vercel env add NPM_TOKEN production --sensitive and paste it there, then the same for preview. Never paste it in chat.

env.learn: Obsidian notes: setup - Secret vs Config; setup - Keys and expiry

probes.name: production editor answers
probes.ifFails: Production isn't serving: check the latest production deployment and the domain on the link-sharing-app project (agent).

ignore.reason: Provisioned on the project by the existing Postgres (Neon) integration, not set by hand; the doctor reports integration values as info.
